quests.question: The candidate ___ we interviewed had great references.
quests.hint: Hidden clause: 'we interviewed ___.' A candidate for a job is a person.
quests.explanation: The candidate is the object of 'interviewed', and because a candidate is a person, 'who' is the correct pronoun.

quests.question: The trailer ___ I watched made the movie look amazing.
quests.hint: Hidden clause: 'I watched ___.' A film trailer is a thing.
quests.explanation: Since the trailer is the object of 'watched' and is a thing, 'which' is correct, not 'who'.

quests.question: The therapist ___ I see every week is very patient.
quests.hint: Hidden clause: 'I see ___ every week.' A therapist is a person you see.
quests.explanation: The therapist is the object of 'see', and since a therapist is a person, the pronoun must be 'who'.

quests.question: The blanket ___ I knitted took me a month.
quests.hint: Hidden clause: 'I knitted ___.' A blanket is a thing you make.
quests.explanation: The blanket is the object of 'knitted'. As a thing, it takes 'which', not a pronoun reserved for people.

quests.question: The agent ___ I booked through gave me a discount.
quests.hint: The preposition 'through' is stranded at the end - trace it back to the person it refers to.
quests.explanation: Even though 'through' is left at the end, its object is the agent, a person, so 'who' is the correct pronoun.

quests.question: The bag ___ I picked turned out to be fake.
quests.hint: Hidden clause: 'I picked ___.' A bag is a thing being chosen.
quests.explanation: Since the bag is the object of 'picked' and is a thing, 'which' is correct rather than 'why'.

quests.question: The sister ___ I trust most lives abroad.
quests.hint: Hidden clause: 'I trust ___ most.' A sister is a person.
quests.explanation: The sister is the object of 'trust', and since she is a person, 'who' is needed instead of 'which'.

quests.question: The project ___ we submitted received the highest grade.
quests.hint: Hidden clause: 'we submitted ___.' A school project is a thing.
quests.explanation: The project is the object of 'submitted'. As a thing, it takes 'which', not a time word like 'when'.

quests.question: The caller ___ I spoke to refused to leave a number.
quests.hint: The preposition 'to' is stranded at the end of the clause - its object is still a person.
quests.explanation: Although 'to' appears at the end, its object is the caller, a person, so the pronoun 'who' is correct.

quests.question: The cake ___ I baked yesterday collapsed in the oven.
quests.hint: A cake isn't a person, so rule out every people-only option before choosing.
quests.explanation: 'That' is a natural, everyday alternative to 'which' for things in object position. 'Who' and 'whose' are impossible since a cake is not a person.

quests.question: The phone ___ I bought last year still works perfectly.
quests.hint: Phones aren't people - eliminate the people-only pronouns first.
quests.explanation: Because a phone is a thing, 'that' works naturally as the object pronoun here. 'Who' could never apply to an object.

quests.question: The colleague ___ I trained left the company.
quests.hint: A colleague is a person - but 'which' can never describe a person, so cross that one out immediately.
quests.explanation: 'That' is a common, neutral way to refer to a person in object position. 'Which' is impossible because it never refers to people.

quests.question: This is the best concert ___ I have ever attended.
quests.hint: You've seen this pattern before: a superlative like 'best' pulls in one particular connector instead of 'which'.
quests.explanation: After superlatives such as 'the best', natural English strongly prefers 'that' over 'which', the same pattern you practiced with subjects earlier.

quests.question: That was the hardest test ___ I have ever taken.
quests.hint: Same superlative pattern as before - 'hardest' behaves just like 'best'.
quests.explanation: 'The hardest' is a superlative, and superlatives are conventionally followed by 'that' rather than 'which' in natural English.

quests.question: This is the only city ___ I would love to live in.
quests.hint: 'Only' triggers the same connector you've now seen several times with superlatives.
quests.explanation: Just like superlatives, 'the only' is followed by 'that' rather than 'which' in idiomatic English.

quests.question: Everything ___ I packed fit into one suitcase.
quests.hint: Indefinite words like 'everything' call for the same connector as before - not 'which'.
quests.explanation: After indefinite pronouns such as 'everything', English speakers naturally use 'that' rather than 'which'.

quests.question: Nothing ___ the doctors tried seemed to help.
quests.hint: Same family of trigger words as 'everything' - apply the same rule.
quests.explanation: 'Nothing' belongs to the same group of indefinite pronouns that prefer 'that' over 'which'.

quests.question: Anything ___ you say will be recorded.
quests.hint: This indefinite word follows the same pattern you've now seen three times.
quests.explanation: Like 'everything' and 'nothing', the word 'anything' is naturally followed by 'that' instead of 'which'.

quests.question: I thanked the stylist and the products ___ transformed my look.
quests.hint: The subject names a person and some things together - one connector has to cover both.
quests.explanation: Because 'the stylist and the products' mixes a person with things, only 'that' can refer to both - 'who' would leave out the products, and 'which' would leave out the stylist.

quests.question: I will never forget the people and the memories ___ shaped my childhood.
quests.hint: Again, the antecedent combines people and things, so only one connector works for both.
quests.explanation: Since 'the people and the memories' combines a person-category with a thing-category, 'that' is needed to refer to both at once.

quests.question: This is the most useful tool ___ the team has built.
quests.hint: A superlative shows up again - recall which connector that pattern favors.
quests.explanation: Following the superlative 'the most useful', 'that' is the natural choice over 'which', continuing the pattern from earlier levels.

quests.question: The captain ___ I spoke to reassured the passengers.
quests.hint: The preposition 'to' is stranded at the end, but its object is still a person.
quests.explanation: Even with 'to' left at the end, its object is the captain, a person, so 'who' is correct.

quests.question: The update ___ I installed fixed the bug.
quests.hint: Hidden clause: 'I installed ___.' A software update is a thing.
quests.explanation: The update is the object of 'installed'. As a thing, it takes 'which', not 'when'.

quests.question: This is the funniest show ___ I have watched all year.
quests.hint: A superlative ('funniest') appears again - the same rule from earlier levels applies.
quests.explanation: After the superlative 'the funniest', 'that' is the conventional choice instead of 'which'.

quests.question: The mentor ___ I admire gave me great advice.
quests.hint: Hidden clause: 'I admire ___.' A mentor is a person.
quests.explanation: The mentor is the object of 'admire', and since a mentor is a person, 'who' is required.

quests.question: The receipt ___ I kept proved the purchase.
quests.hint: Hidden clause: 'I kept ___.' A receipt is a thing.
quests.explanation: The receipt is the object of 'kept'. As a thing, it takes 'which' rather than 'who'.

quests.question: All ___ I wanted was a quiet evening.
quests.hint: 'All' behaves like the indefinite words you practiced earlier (everything, nothing, anything).
quests.explanation: Like 'everything' and 'nothing', the word 'all' is conventionally followed by 'that' rather than 'which'.

quests.question: The supplier ___ we chose offered the best price.
quests.hint: Hidden clause: 'we chose ___.' A supplier here refers to a person or company representative acting as one.
quests.explanation: The supplier is the object of 'chose', and since the supplier is treated as a person here, 'who' is correct.

quests.question: The supplement ___ I take every morning boosts my energy.
quests.hint: Hidden clause: 'I take ___ every morning.' A supplement is a thing.
quests.explanation: The supplement is the object of 'take'. As a thing, 'which' is correct, not a time word.

quests.question: This is the clearest explanation ___ I have ever read.
quests.hint: Superlative pattern one more time - 'clearest' behaves exactly like 'best' or 'funniest'.
quests.explanation: Following the superlative 'the clearest', 'that' completes the pattern you've now practiced across many levels.
